ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy set with scorching Let It Grow and epic Earthquake Space
ai_show_review.blurb: The Hartford show bursts open with a searing Bertha and rides through tight classics like Althea and Big Railroad Blues. The second set erupts into an unforgettable sequence – Playing In The Band > Eyes Of The World, Phil’s earthquake‑laden Space, and a rare Playing In The Band > Sugar Magnolia combo. Across all sources the band is locked in, delivering one of ’82’s most electric performances.
ai_show_review.review:
What unfolds at the Hartford Civic Center on April 18, 1982 is a textbook example of late‑career Dead brilliance. The first set lays down a solid groove with Jerry’s razor‑sharp solo on Bertha, a fiery Let It Grow that many reviewers call “ripping,” and Brent’s Hammond chops driving Big Railroad Blues into overdrive. Phil’s bass provides the perfect counterpoint, especially during his legendary “Earthquake” segment of Space, where the rhythm section builds an almost tectonic swell.

The second set is where the night truly shines: a seamless transition from Playing In The Band into Eyes Of The World sets up a soaring jam that bursts through the Rhythm Devils’ tight drumming before Phil launches his earthquake‑filled Space. That segues into The Other One, then a patient yet inspiring Black Peter, and finally a rare, high‑octane combo of Sugar Magnolia > Playing In The Band that keeps the momentum sky‑high all the way to Sunshine Daydream. Brent’s organ textures on Cold Rain And Snow and his gritty Hammond work on Big Railroad Blues add depth, while Mickey and Bill lock in with crisp snare depth and relentless drive. In short, this show captures the band at a creative peak – tight, adventurous, and utterly exhilarating.

best_recording.reason: Pristine soundboard capture with crystal‑clear mix, no dropouts, and full band balance – the definitive source for this high‑energy performance

key_highlights: Scorching Let It Grow solo that defines the night
Epic Phil’s Earthquake Space sequence with thunderous bass
Rare Playing In The Band > Sugar Magnolia combo in the second set
Tight, patient jam through The Other One and Black Peter
Brent’s Hammond brilliance on Big Railroad Blues

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers ripping solos – especially on Let It Grow and Bertha – with a warm, seasoned vocal that sits front‑and‑center throughout the night.
band_performance.Phil: Anchors the jams with his trademark “quake” bass during Space; despite occasional low mix in audience tapes his playing drives the improvisations.
band_performance.Bob: Provides solid rhythm guitar work, slide on Samson & Delilah and strong vocal delivery on Ship Of Fools, keeping the band grounded.
band_performance.Brent: Adds gritty Hammond organ on Big Railroad Blues and lush church‑organ texture on Cold Rain And Snow; his keyboards are a key driver of the set’s power.
band_performance.Mickey: Locks in with tight, propulsive patterns that fuel the Rhythm Devils’ intensity, especially evident during the Space/Earthquake climax.
band_performance.Billy: Offers crisp snare depth and a steady foundation, giving the second‑set jams extra weight and clarity.
